WORKED EXAMPLE: FINDING MONOPOLY PRICE

runs.text: Price / cost ($) is vertical; Quantity is horizontal. MR crosses MC at quantity 40 and $20. Demand gives price $40 at that quantity; ATC is $45. The demand-MC intersection near quantity 67 and $27 is not the monopoly output choice.

transcript.sourceText: The monopolist first finds output where MR = MC, which occurs at 40 units and a marginal value of $20. It then moves up to the demand curve, where buyers will pay $40 for 40 units. The profit-maximizing choice is therefore Q = 40 and P = $40, not the $20 MR value.
transcript.text: The monopolist first finds output where M R equals M C , which occurs at 40 units and a marginal value of 20 dollars . It then moves up to the demand curve, where buyers will pay 40 dollars for 40 units. The profit-maximizing choice is therefore Q equals 40 and P equals 40 dollars , not the 20 dollars MR value.
